subject: chemistry
title: Properties of ionic compounds
key_idea: Ionic compounds have high melting and boiling points because many strong electrostatic forces must be overcome. They conduct electricity when molten or dissolved, because the ions are then free to move. They do not conduct when solid.

blocks.text: Ionic compounds are solids at room temperature with high melting points. This section covers why, in three parts that every answer needs.

items.text: An ionic compound is a giant lattice of oppositely charged ions.
There are strong electrostatic forces of attraction between the oppositely charged ions, acting in all directions.
A large amount of energy is needed to overcome these forces, so the melting and boiling points are high.

items: Ionic solids are hard but brittle.
Many dissolve in water, but not all of them do.
Metal chlorides are usually ionic, so they are usually solids at room temperature with high melting points.
Giant lattice, strong electrostatic forces in all directions, large amount of energy.
Ionic compounds have high melting and boiling points.
The forces overcome are between ions. No molecules are involved.

blocks.text: A substance conducts electricity when it has charged particles that are free to move. This section covers when an ionic compound does and does not.

rows: Fixed in the lattice, only vibrating

diagram.alt: Sort each state of an ionic compound into conducts electricity or does not conduct.
diagram.prompt: Does it conduct electricity? Sort each one.

items: The charge is carried by the **ions**, not by electrons.
In a solid the ions cannot move, so no charge flows.
Metals conduct as solids because they have delocalised electrons. An ionic solid has none.
Ionic compounds conduct when molten or dissolved, because the ions are free to move.
They do not conduct as solids, because the ions are held in fixed positions.

checks.q: Explain why sodium chloride has a high melting point.
checks.a: It is a giant ionic lattice with strong electrostatic forces between oppositely charged ions. A lot of energy is needed to overcome them.

checks.q: Give two ways to make solid sodium chloride conduct electricity.
checks.a: Melt it, or dissolve it in water.

checks.q: Gallium oxide has a very high melting point. It does not conduct as a solid but does when molten. Name the type of substance.

worked_example.question: A substance conducts electricity when it has charged particles that are free to move. Explain why sodium chloride conducts electricity when molten but not when solid.
answer_points: Which are free to move when molten.
But are fixed in the solid.
worked_example.tip: Charged particles is allowed for the second and third points, but name the ions for the first.

worked_example.question: Sodium carbonate has the formula Na₂CO₃. Sodium carbonate contains Na⁺ ions and CO₃²⁻ ions. Explain why solid sodium carbonate cannot conduct electricity but a solution of sodium carbonate can conduct electricity.
answer_points: In the solid the ions are in an ionic lattice, held by strong electrostatic attractions.
So the ions cannot move, they are fixed or just vibrate.
In solution the ions can move, they are free.
worked_example.tip: Electrons and intermolecular forces are rejected. Say ions throughout.

worked_example.question: A scientist uses data about four substances to find out what type of bonding each one has. Substance A: melting point 550 °C, boiling point 1300 °C, soluble in water, does not conduct as a solid, conducts when molten or dissolved. Substance B: melting point -183 °C, boiling point -162 °C, not soluble, does not conduct in any state. Substance C: melting point 420 °C, boiling point 907 °C, not soluble, conducts as a solid and when molten or dissolved. Substance D: melting point 1670 °C, boiling point above 1670 °C, not soluble, does not conduct in any state. The scientist thinks substance A is an ionic compound. Explain why the scientist is correct.
answer_points: Ionic compounds have high melting and boiling points, and A has a high melting point of 550 °C and boiling point of 1300 °C.
Ionic compounds conduct when molten or dissolved, but not as a solid, which is what A does.
worked_example.tip: Quote the data from the table and link it to the property of ionic compounds.
